`Logger` implements PSR-3 and writes formatted records from a background task. Use it in CLI servers and
workers that need logging to return even when standard error or another destination is slow.

## Installation

```shell
composer require thesis/logger
```

Requires 64-bit PHP 8.6+.

## Usage

```php
use Thesis\Async\Group;
use Thesis\Logger;
use function Thesis\Async\group;
use function Thesis\Io\stderr;

group(static function (Group $group) {
    $logger = new Logger(stderr());
    $logger->run($group);

    try {
        $logger->info('Worker {worker} is ready', ['worker' => 3]);
    } finally {
        $logger->close();
    }
});
```

## Output formats

`Formatter\Json` is the default. Each NDJSON line has `time` (RFC 3339 with microseconds), `level`, `message`
and a `context` object. Scalar fields keep their JSON types.

Use `Formatter\Console` for a text line with a timestamp, a colored level label, the message and any context.
Pass `colors: false` for plain text.

```php
use Thesis\Logger\Formatter\Console;

$logger = new Logger(stderr(), formatter: new Console());
```

Implement `Formatter::format(Record $record)` to provide your own format. The writer task calls it with the
`DateTimeImmutable` captured at the log call, the interpolated message and the normalized context.
Return one line. `Logger` adds `\n` and counts output as dropped if it contains a line break or exceeds 16 KiB
including the terminator.

## Time and timezone

`Logger` reads its PSR-20 `ClockInterface` in the calling fiber. The default `Thesis\Time\WallClock` uses the
PHP default timezone. Both built-in formatters preserve the offset returned by the clock. Pass your own clock
to control the timestamp, or use `WallClock` with a fixed timezone.

```php
use Thesis\Time\WallClock;

$logger = new Logger(stderr(), clock: new WallClock(new DateTimeZone('UTC')));
```

## Messages and context

Scalar context values fill matching `{key}` placeholders in every format. Missing keys stay in the message.
The context keeps its fields after interpolation. An exception under
`exception` becomes an object with `type`, `message`, `file` and `line`. Other objects, arrays and resources in the context
are represented by their type. A `Stringable` message is cast to a string on the calling fiber.
Non-finite floats are written as `null`. Context is capped at 32 entries, keys at 128 bytes and
text at 1024 bytes.

## Buffering and shutdown

The default minimum level is `info` and the default queue holds 1024 lines. Pass `minLevel` or `capacity`
to change these. A full queue drops the incoming record. `$dropped` counts records refused or lost, including
before `run()` or after `close()`. Records filtered by level do not count.

Read `$logger->failure` to check whether formatting or writing stopped the background task. It holds the
original throwable as soon as the writer catches it, and `close()` rethrows it. Queue overflow, normal
shutdown and task cancellation leave this property null.

Stop producers first and then call `close()` while the group is still running. `close()` stops accepting
records and drains the queue. It leaves the destination open and throws if formatting or writing failed. In a cancelled
scope use `shield()` with a `timeout()` to give the writer time to drain. A cancelled wait leaves the writer
free to continue until the group ends, and a later `close()` can wait for it again.
